NEW FILE, claims 0 lines -- it ports no JS, it fixes a port defect. Shared clear for the city's 'nothing is baked, OnEnable -> EnsureBuilt regenerates' contract. MEASURED DEFECT: every scenery renderer is [ExecuteAlways] with OnEnable -> EnsureBuilt, but only ShopfrontRenderer.ClearChildren walked real Transform children. ParkRenderer's and LandmarkRenderer's cleared a private List<GameObject> _children -- a private field is not serialised, so a SCENE LOAD leaves it empty while the deserialised children are right there -- and MetroRenderer, MallRenderer and StreetFurnitureRenderer had no clear at all. The baked copies therefore survived the load and the fresh build was added alongside them: the Buildings root held 2,735 descendants after loading the baked scene against 1,771 after loading a stripped one, ~964 objects co-located and drawn twice, with 2.50 GB peak load memory. GeneratedChildren.Clear(root, disposeRuntimeAssets) destroys every real Transform child (ShopfrontRenderer's pattern, plain DestroyImmediate in edit mode, never Undo.DestroyObjectImmediate -- an undo record per object is pointless for regenerated geometry) and optionally reclaims the non-persistent Meshes/Materials/Texture2Ds those children referenced, skipping anything EditorUtility.IsPersistent owns so it can never eat an imported FBX/OBJ asset. All eight renderers call it: Park/Landmark/Mall with disposal (per-build meshes, MatLambert/MatWater/clamped-clone materials, 42 rasterised 1024x128 mall sign plates), Shopfront without (bit-for-bit its old behaviour; SignPool owns its slots), Metro without (its _matCache and _nameBoardMesh are static, built once per domain -- and both were hardened to tolerate a destroyed object: `&& hit != null` on the three _matCache lookups and `if (_nameBoardMesh == null)` instead of `??=`, because C#'s null-coalescing does not see Unity's destroyed-object null and would return a corpse forever), and City/Vegetation/StreetFurniture as insurance -- those three create ZERO Transform children (everything is a Matrix4x4 in _batches) so they were never part of the double-draw, but a private _batches guard means a load always re-enters EnsureBuilt and the uniform contract is the only defence against a future child-creating pass. Each renderer also gained an internal RebuildForCheck() that clears its build guard (and empties _children WITHOUT destroying, reproducing a fresh component) and re-runs EnsureBuilt. PROVEN by Editor/SceneryRebuildCheck.cs against the real Assets/Scenes/Game.unity: pass1==pass2 for all eight (City 0/0, Shopfront 195/195, Vegetation 0/0, Park 224/224, Metro 557/557, Mall 84/84, StreetFurniture 0/0, Landmark 96/96), REBUILDCHECK_RESULT checked=8 doubled=0, and every renderer's own count line repeats identically on the second build (METRORENDERER spawned=106, MALLRENDERER spawned=84).
